data.description:
## The hazard, and it already caused a live incident

`git stash` writes to the SHARED git common dir, not to the worktree. On this host there are
roughly 30 worktrees with multiple agents working concurrently, so the stash is a single global
stack that every agent pushes to and pops from.

Two agents stashing at overlapping times will pop EACH OTHER'S uncommitted work into the wrong
worktree.

## Confirmed incident 2026-08-05

An agent working bug c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af used `git stash` twice to check whether a test failure
was pre-existing. On the second use a concurrent agent's stash operation interleaved, and it
popped the OTHER agent's changes into its worktree while its own went to theirs.

It recovered only because it happened to hold out-of-band copies. The displaced work was
preserved two ways and is STILL SITTING THERE at time of filing:

    stash@{0}: On fix-c5b3-scc-byfile: RECOVERED measurement-provenance work
               (ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance) displaced into worktree
               fix-c5b3-scc-byfile by a shared-stash race;
               backup at /tmp/RECOVERED-stash-race

ACTION NEEDED INDEPENDENT OF THIS BUG: that is another session's work on ADR 0061 /
det_measurement_provenance. Whoever owns it likely does not know it was displaced. It should be
returned to its owner before anything prunes the stash or clears /tmp.

## Why this is a rebar problem and not just a git fact

rebar's own guidance actively produces the conditions for it. AGENTS.md mandates working in
fresh worktrees, and `make worktree` makes spinning them up a single command. The
parallel-agent workflow is a documented, encouraged pattern. So the project tells agents to run
many worktrees in parallel while `git stash` — a reflex command for "let me check this against
a clean tree" — is silently global across all of them.

The failure is also SILENT and DESTRUCTIVE: `git stash pop` succeeds, the wrong files appear,
and nothing indicates the content came from another worktree. An agent that then commits has
committed someone else's work; an agent whose changes vanished may conclude its edits were
never made.

## What agents should do instead (all worktree-local)

- A throwaway worktree for the clean-tree comparison:
  `git worktree add /tmp/<unique> origin/main --detach`
- `git archive <ref>` to materialize a specific tree shape (ticket 7e90's agent did exactly
  this successfully to reproduce a pre-gate `.github/` layout).
- `git diff > /tmp/<unique>.patch` + `git checkout -- <paths>`, re-applied with `git apply`.
- Plain file copies inside the agent's own worktree directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AGENTS.md states plainly that `git stash` is UNSAFE in this repo's parallel-worktree
      workflow, with the worktree-local alternatives above, sited where an agent reaching for
      stash will actually see it (near the worktree/parallel-agent guidance, not an appendix).
- [ ] The reason is given, not just the prohibition — an agent that understands the stash is
      global will generalize; one told a bare rule will work around it.
- [ ] Consider a mechanical block rather than relying on agents reading docs: evaluate whether
      a pre-commit or wrapper can refuse `git stash` when more than one worktree exists, and
      either implement it or record why not.
- [ ] The displaced ADR 0061 work above is returned to its owner or confirmed no longer needed,
      and the stash entry and /tmp backup are cleaned up only after that.
- [ ] Sweep for other git commands with the same shared-common-dir property and document any
      found (hooks are already known-shared — bug 84aa records a worktree-wide hook clobber
      from the same root cause, which suggests this class is recurring).

## Provenance

Reported by the agent that hit it while working c5b3. Bug 84aa is prior art for the same class:
hooks live in the shared common dir, so installing one from a linked worktree clobbered it for
every worktree at once.
data.title: git stash is SHARED across all worktrees, so parallel agents silently swap each other's uncommitted work
